title: Ultimate Trickery
problem: The transform sets the creature id, class, race and sprite of the copied species, so the holder counts as that species for every species check (e.g. perks keyed to a creature id). That is what "transforms into a copy" means. It keeps its own innate trait (Ultimate Trickery) and appends the 3rd creature's innate and the 4th creature's fused trait to its extra traits. The fake-Animatus case cannot arise on your side: the Animatus is always in party slot 1, and Ultimate Trickery copies slot 2.
notes: Text: At the start of battle, this creature transforms into a copy of the second creature in your party, gains the innate trait of the third creature in your party, and gains the fused ... Evidence: bc_StartupTraits L277-L287: gate @0x1417745e8, crits[2] must exist and not be the holder (L278), bc_EventTransform(holder, crits[2].critconstant, holder.passive) queued @0x141774a34; L283 crits[3].passive and L287 crits[4].passive2 appended to extrapassives; enemy branch L291-L294 uses enemies[]. Transform applied in bc_ExecuteEvents @0x1410b2613-0x1410b4500 (critconstant, class, race, sprite). Animator perks test creature id 955. Reasoning: A copy that carries the copied creature id is the literal meaning of the text; species-keyed perks applying to it follows from that. Nothing to change. Source: errata round 2 (2026-10-26).
